input.quote: Section 8.3 Termination. This Agreement will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a) the date upon which the last remaining Receivable is paid in full, settled, sold or written off and any amounts received are applied and (b) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full (Section 8.3) — well beyond twelve months — yet the only exit against the Servicer is the for-cause removal right in Section 7.2(c), exercisable by the Indenture Trustee upon a continuing Servicer Termination Event. Sections 8.1 and 8.2 are Certificateholder optional acquisition/redemption mechanics, not a convenience termination right for us. There is therefore no Customer convenience exit at all, which fails both the preferred and fallback positions (fallback element 1 is likewise absent, and there is no early-termination fee to cap). We target the preferred level: Section 7.1 already bars the Servicer from resigning absent legal inability, so the Vendor-side element is met and the fallback (which would let the Servicer walk at term end on 90 days' notice) would weaken us. The single inserted Section 7.7 supplies the Issuer's 30-day convenience right and pro rata refund of prepaid fees; existing Sections 7.3 and 7.4 already handle continued performance and successor engagement on any termination "under this Agreement", so no consequential edits are needed.

ops.text: Termination for Convenience. The Issuer may terminate this Agreement and the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer, in which case the Servicer will refund pro rata any fees prepaid for the period after the effective date of the termination.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a convenience exit for the Issuer on thirty (30) days' notice with a pro rata refund of any prepaid fees, since the Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid and today only gives us a for-cause removal right. Section 7.1 already bars the Servicer from resigning, so no change is needed on that side.
proposal.summary: Add an Issuer right to terminate the Agreement for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro rata refund of prepaid fees.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
mappings.quote: The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
